text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The Democratic Party Saimnieks, the largest party in the government, decided to recall its three state ministers from their posts. The party also called for getting rid of all the state minister and deputy prime minister posts, going further than Prime Minister Andris Shkele, who wanted to get rid of only a few state minister jobs. Saimnieks said the money saved could be spent in other areas in the budget.
- President Guntis Ulmanis will leave on November 7 for his first official visit to Britain.
- The government's economic panel aproved a draft law on giving the port of Ventspils the status of a free port. The draft is scheduled to take effect on Jaunuary 1, 1997.
- Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans said that Aeroflot flights to Riga were stopped on October 31 because the Russian side did not observe the principle of parity.
- The economics ministry submitted to the cabinet a project to promote regional development.

- The Latvian foreign ministry will certainly respond if the Lithuanian parliament unilaterally adopts a law delimiting the sea border with Latvia. The two neighbours have been involved in a long-running row over their sea border after Latvia signed an exploration deal with Amoco in waters where the border has still not been determined.

- One of Banka Baltija's liquidators told a news conference that since starting the liquidation of the bank three months ago, they have spent 75,000 lats or 2.8 percent of the sum currently available in Banka Baltija.
